decision: The team builds a reading-list panel that loads three sample sources and holds its layout through every state.
plan:
## Pitch

**Dance choreographer:** Strip it to the panel. A reading list loads, sits there, or breaks. The sample record lives in one place and the view only reads it. Six parts that each show one moment: the skeleton, the wait, the failure, the retry, the list, the tabs that switch sources. What does the visitor do with each one? If a part gives them nothing to do or nothing to read, it goes.

**Railway signaller:** A source board. Three feeds sit on one panel, and each tab carries a signal aspect: pending, clear, failed. Every tab follows the same rule. Same glyph slot, same width, same 8px gap. Components: aspect tabs, a skeleton block, a failure plate, a retry lever, a list, a last-good timestamp. The material is the row height. Keep it fixed and the panel holds still.

**Optical technician:** Make it strange. The skeleton develops like a print in a tray, rows coming up out of grey. Who needs cancel, who needs retry? Pending past eight seconds needs cancel. Failed needs retry. Cancelled needs both. And test the longest label, "Timed out after 6 s · showing copy from 14:02". The plate is sized from that string.

**Satellite repair apprentice:** I'd take the team card's share sheet. Copy link, report clipboard failure, close by swipe, button or Escape. It's the bottom-sheet source. Fewer parts: sheet, copy row, failure line. Press copy twice and see whether it says the same thing both times. If it doesn't, nobody will trust it.

## Clash

**Satellite repair apprentice:** The share sheet has a failure state too. Clipboard denied. Isn't that the same lesson?

**Dance choreographer:** The brief says request loader. Pending, loaded, failed, retry. Your sheet has no pending phase worth a component. It's a good piece for another day.

**Satellite repair apprentice:** Fine. Then retry has to survive a double press. Two clicks, one request. Second click reads "Retrying", nothing else.

**Optical technician:** The developing skeleton is my strange part. It shows the shape of what's coming before it comes.

**Railway signaller:** Animated grey rows change brightness at different times. That reads as uneven. A static block at the final row height does the real job. No layout shift.

**Optical technician:** Then the strangeness goes somewhere honest. The failure plate keeps the last good list visible underneath, dimmed and stamped with its time. The panel stays full and you can still read the old copy.

**Dance choreographer:** That plate overlaps the pending indicator. Who owns "Still waiting"?

**Optical technician:** Pending owns time. The plate owns cause. Cancel lives on pending after 8 s. Retry lives on the plate. Neither one says the other's line.

**Railway signaller:** And selection in the list uses the tab rule. One 2px left bar, accent, the same everywhere. No second treatment.

## Decision

The team builds a reading-list panel that loads three sample sources and holds its layout through every state. The visitor can cancel a slow request or retry a failed one without losing the last good copy.

Concept: Holding Panel

The choreographer set the boundary. One store per source feeds six views, and every part answers "what can I do here". The signaller fixed the material: 56px rows, a 24px glyph slot on tabs, one selection rule across tabs and list, and every gap drawn from a 4/8/16/24 scale. The optical technician split cancel from retry by state and sized the failure plate from its longest label. The technician also kept the dimmed last-good list under the failure plate. The apprentice made the Archive outcome deterministic and added the double-press guard on retry, so every action gives the same result on a second test.

Rejected direction: the share sheet from the team card. It has merit, but the edition brief and the issue scope ask for a request loader. The feed item on CSS `random()` was also set aside, because random skeleton widths would undercut stable layout.

Source: https://github.com/isas1/creative-sites-vault/blob/1595af38a69fbb67c674ef4b90b776a2245c270b/00-components/loaders/05-dash-orbital-ring/var-1-arc-spinner.html. The retained mechanism is the rotating top-border arc on a 2px ring, used only in row 2. The team makes three improvements:
1. The source declares `role=status` on both the host and the inner div. The rebuild puts one polite live region on a text line that reads "Waiting · 3 s", and only that line is announced.
2. Under reduced motion, the source stops the ring, which leaves a shape that looks finished. The rebuild draws a static three-quarter arc and keeps the word "Waiting".
3. The source spins forever in hardcoded white. The rebuild waits 400 ms before showing, takes its colour from tokens, adds Cancel at 8 s and unmounts on loaded or failed.

Six components earn their place because each one covers a separate state or job. A seventh candidate, an outcome switch for the demo, was cut. The Archive source fails once by design, so the demo needs no extra test control.

## Build notes

1. Define spacing once as `--s1: 4px; --s2: 8px; --s3: 16px; --s4: 24px`. Every margin, gap and padding in all six files uses only these values. Row height is 56px, which is 16 + 24 + 16.
2. Archive is deterministic: a timeout at 6000 ms on attempt 1 and success on attempt 2. Press Retry twice inside 100 ms and confirm that the request id increments once and the list renders once.
3. At 320px width, test the plate with "Timed out after 6 s · showing copy from 14:02" and the longest sample title. Both must wrap without truncation and keep the panel's min-height. Measure layout stability with a ResizeObserver log. This pack does not claim stability from inspection.

components.name: Retry guard
components.description: Retry button with a reserved label width, attempt count and a double-press guard.
components.purpose: Start one new attempt for a failed or cancelled source.
components.use: A reader presses Retry on Archive twice by accident, and one request runs.
components.input: Click or tap Retry. Keyboard: Tab to it, Enter or Space, or R while the panel has focus.
components.outcome: Attempt n+1 starts. The label reads 'Retrying' and the button disables until the request settles.
components.recovery: If attempt 2 also fails, the label returns to 'Retry' with 'Attempt 2 failed'. Focus returns to the button.
components.mechanism: A request id increments per attempt. Presses while a request is in flight are ignored. Replies with an older id are dropped. Label width is reserved from the longest label, 'Retrying'.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-27 pipeline panel retried a build step. This retry adds a double-press guard and stale-reply dropping for a content request.
components.usefulness: Double taps on slow networks are common, and duplicate requests cause flicker and wrong content.
components.creativeDifference: The button reports the attempt number, so a second failure reads as new information.
states: ready: 'Retry', reached on failed or cancelled
retrying: disabled 'Retrying', reached on press
ignored: second press during retrying, no change
failed-again: 'Retry' with 'Attempt 2 failed', reached by a second failure
hidden: not rendered when loaded or empty
focus: 2px ring

components.name: Failure plate
components.description: Failure notice naming the cause, laid over a dimmed last-good list stamped with its time.
components.purpose: Explain why the load failed and keep previous content readable.
components.use: A reader sees 'Timed out after 6 s · showing copy from 14:02' and keeps reading the old list.
components.input: Click or tap Details to expand the cause. Keyboard: Tab to Details, Enter or Space toggles.
components.outcome: The plate states the cause and the last-good time. Details show the sample source, the attempt and the elapsed time.
components.recovery: Retry in row 4 sits inside the plate. With no last-good data, the plate reads 'Nothing loaded yet' at the same height.
components.mechanism: The plate is a disclosure button and region. The last-good list renders at 0.55 opacity with inert set. The plate width is sized from the longest message, and text wraps on narrow widths without truncation.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-28 load stages reported 'Aggregate failed · kept 6h' in one line. This plate keeps the old content readable and gives it a timestamp.
components.usefulness: A blank panel on failure throws away content the reader already had.
components.creativeDifference: Failure shows as a layer over still-readable old content, so the panel keeps its height and its use.
states: timed-out: 'Timed out after 6 s', reached on Archive attempt 1
cancelled: 'Cancelled at 9 s', reached by row 2 Cancel
with-last-good: dimmed list plus timestamp
no-last-good: 'Nothing loaded yet'
details-open: cause, attempt and elapsed time shown
focus: 2px ring on Details

components.name: Loaded list
components.description: Article list with a single selection rule, a loaded-at line and an empty result.
components.purpose: Show the loaded items and let the reader pick one.
components.use: A reader opens 'Field notes on rail signalling' from Inbox.
components.input: Click or tap a row. Keyboard: Tab into the list, Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter selects.
components.outcome: The selected row gets the 2px accent left bar. The footer reads 'Loaded 12 · 14:06'. Focus moves to the list heading after load only if the reader triggered the load.
components.recovery: Selection survives a reload when the item id still exists. Otherwise it clears with 'Selection no longer in list'.
components.mechanism: A listbox with roving tabindex. Rows reuse the row 3 grid template at 56px. Titles clamp to 2 lines and the full title sits in a title attribute and the accessible name. Shared returns zero items and renders 'No shared articles' at row height.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-26 log viewer event list filtered events by severity. This list is the arrival point of a request and keeps selection across reloads.
components.usefulness: This list is the reason the panel exists.
components.creativeDifference: The selection mark is shared with the source tabs, so one visual rule reads across the panel.
states: loaded: rows with footer count and time
selected: 2px accent left bar, reached by click or Enter
focus: row ring, reached by arrows
empty: 'No shared articles', reached on Shared
selection-cleared: note shown, reached when a reload drops the selected id
long-title: two-line clamp with full accessible name

demo.sharedState: One store keyed by source id (inbox, shared, archive), each holding {status, attempt, requestId, startedAt, items, lastGood, lastGoodAt, error}. Row 1 reads status for glyphs and sets the active source. Rows 2 and 3 render while status is pending. Row 2 Cancel aborts and sets status to cancelled. Rows 4 and 5 render on failed or cancelled. Row 4 dispatches load(source) with attempt+1. Row 6 renders items on loaded or empty. Inbox loads 12 items in 1.2 s. Shared returns 0 in 0.8 s. Archive times out at 6 s on attempt 1 and returns 9 items in 1.5 s on attempt 2. Views never write to each other, only to the store.
